newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tension reigns as German shares try to find floor.
newsitem.headline: Tension reigns as German shares try to find floor.

text.p: German shares were hovering little changed in late electronic dealings on Thursday, buoyed by ongoing interest in utility RWE AG, but dealers said the market was still extremely nervous.
"My nerves are shattered," said a Frankfurt dealer.
"We've all been caught wrongfooted. I am getting constant calls from nervous investors and lots of them don't want to do anything at all," he added.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was up 8.54 points at 4,245.46 points at 1344 GMT, calming slightly after a brief tremor following U.S. data that was broadly in line with forecasts.
Prices have veered in a 90-point band on the IBIS DAX today, but appeared to hold firm above the 4,200-point mark which many dealers view as psychologically crucial.

Opinions were sharply divided as to the market's likely next move, with some dealers predicting a further slide in prices as fears about an interest rate hike mount, while others said an imminent monetary tightening was priced in and the market could soon resume its rally.
Developments on the Dow Jones Index were universally viewed as crucial, however. The index's fall below the key 8,000 point level unsettled many European investors.
The Dow opened higher in Europe's afternoon trading hours, but dealers were still wary that its trend could change completely mid-session.

The only clear bright spark on the horizon was utility RWE AG, which on Wednesday night announced plans to shelve an unpopular system of multiple voting rights attached to shares held mainly by local municipalities.
The move was viewed as opening up the company to international investors, by loosening old ties on its equity.
RWE preferred shares were trading up 14.5 percent at 75.80 marks while its common stock was up 12 percent at 89.50 marks.
Holders of preferred shares in RWE will be invited to swap these for common shares under the new voting rights system.
Prefered shares in Volkswagen AG rose 39.50 marks, or four percent, at 984.50 marks as investors hoped a similar system to RWE's might be introduced in their case.
Elsewhere chemical shares remained under pressure after a badly-received earnings report from BASF AG.
Hoechst AG was down 4.60 marks, or nearly six percent, at 75.90 marks, while BASF was down 3.36 marks, or 4.7 percent, at 68.14 marks.
Bayer AG was more stable, down 2.40 marks at 73.60 marks.
BASF said its pre-tax profits rose nearly six percent to 2.46 billion marks, at the lower end of expectations.
